title: Issues tried by consent
summary: An issue not stated in the pleadings may become part of the case when the parties expressly or impliedly consent to trying it. The evidence and conduct of the parties must support that conclusion.
notes: The mere admission of evidence relevant to two issues does not automatically add an unpleaded claim.

sections.Meaning: An issue not stated in the pleadings may become part of the case when the parties expressly or impliedly consent to trying it. The evidence and conduct of the parties must support that conclusion.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify what additional issue was actually litigated and what notice the opponent had. In Moore, evidence already relevant to child-related issues did not necessarily show consent to try a separate spousal-support claim.
